clue.text: Splash preventer — ruction re wash if out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are disordered, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a fuss is being made about washing done in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges RUCTION, RE and WASH; 'if' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom screen of fabric or plastic stops spray from the shower soaking the floor.

clue.text: 007, say, notwithstanding all the films!

parts.note: Bond's job is supposedly hush-hush, yet he has been splashed across cinema screens for decades

explanation.surface: James Bond is meant to be undercover despite starring in so many films.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond, code number 007, is a spy employed covertly by the British secret service.

clue.text: Always available where C or H is seen?

definitions.meaning: ready to be drawn on whenever wanted, like beer from a barrel

definitions.text: where C or H is seen?
definitions.meaning: C and H mark the cold and hot taps on a basin

explanation.definitionFit: Something readily obtainable is like water from a faucet; and C or H labels a faucet.

clue.text: Initial description of what may be seen as vintage stuff

definitions.text: Initial description of what may be seen as vintage stuff

parts.words: Initial description of what may be seen as vintage stuff
parts.note: a French term for wine bought young, at its earliest stage, before it is bottled and becomes a vintage

explanation.surface: A first account of some old-fashioned material.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French for 'at its first', used of wines sold in advance while still in the cask.
explanation.definitionFit: This French trade phrase describes young wine sold before bottling, its first appearance on the market.

clue.text: Mysterious uproar over picture Times initially included

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above, over, the next

parts.note: an uproar is an outcry, a cry

indicators.note: the first letter of Times is included inside the word for picture

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of Times

explanation.surface: A puzzling commotion about a photograph that included The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the next; 'included' means the T of Times goes inside the picture word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mysterious remark is enigmatic, with a hidden meaning, just like this newspaper's puzzles.

clue.text: Treatment for alcoholism? That chap in pub may be made over

indicators.note: made over means turned over, so the whole assembly is read backwards
that chap's word goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
he refers to that chap

explanation.surface: A drinker in a pub might be transformed by getting help for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub-with-chap gives BAHER, which 'may be made over' turns round; the definition's question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation programmes help people recover from alcohol dependency.

clue.text: Flower a stupid sheep pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue pulled up means read from bottom to top, so these two words run backwards

parts.note: silly means stupid
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A foolish sheep yanked a flower out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' reverses SILLY RAM to give MARYLLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a bulbous plant with large trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: New and old: right to see conjunction

explanation.surface: Something new and something old together make it right to see a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: This word joins clauses as a negative alternative, so grammatically it is a conjunction.

clue.text: Who'd get drunk around start of ceilidh?

definitions.text: Who'd get drunk around start of ceilidh?

indicators.note: the drunkard's word goes around the opening letter of ceilidh

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard, one who would get drunk

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of ceilidh

explanation.surface: Who would be getting tipsy as a Highland dance begins?
explanation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish evening of folk music and dancing; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotsman is the stereotypical reveller at a ceilidh, the Highland dance party.

clue.text: A shrinking area of study?

parts.note: not a field getting smaller but one practised by 'shrinks', slang for mental-health doctors

explanation.surface: A subject that is gradually diminishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychiatrists are nicknamed shrinks, so their medical discipline is a field of shrinking.

clue.text: Close to victory here — ready to engrave one name into trophy?

parts.note: set means ready, as in 'all set'

indicators.note: the letters for one and name go into the trophy word

parts.note: pot is slang for a trophy or cup
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An engraver is all set to add a winner's name to a cup that is nearly won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts I and N inside POT, giving POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the point that would win the set brings a player near to victory.

clue.text: Pay to get rid of expert that's cornered you? Not entirely

indicators.note: the expert's word has trapped the shortened 'you' inside it, as though cornering it

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of you is dropped

parts.note: you is the word being cut short

explanation.surface: Bribe an expert who has trapped you into a corner, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts the last letter off 'you'; 'that's cornered' means the expert word holds those two letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bribe someone to go away is to buy them out of the way, paying to be rid of them.

clue.text: Meteor the cause of a retake?

definitions.meaning: a shooting star streaking across the sky
a film actor tumbling over during a take means the scene must be shot again

explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is popularly called a shooting star; a toppling actor spoils a take.

clue.text: Journalist can be misled about unknown taxi

parts.note: a hack is a journalist

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the unknown
misled means led astray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A reporter may be led astray over a taxi of unknown origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misled' rearranges CAN BE; 'about' puts that around Y to make NEYCAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney carriage is the formal name for a licensed London taxi.

clue.text: Loving technical book

parts.note: an ancient Sanskrit manual whose name joins 'love' with 'treatise', a how-to guide to lovemaking

explanation.surface: A manual for someone who adores technicalities.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Indian text is a practical treatise on sexual love and technique.

clue.text: Display of stoutness? Stout may well come into it

definitions.meaning: a visible sign of being fat, a paunch on show

definitions.text: Stout may well come into it
definitions.meaning: dark beer such as stout is poured into a drinker's paunch

explanation.definitionFit: A paunch shows corpulence, and stout, the dark beer, ends up inside it.

clue.text: Provided illumination about line in tune

indicators.note: the word for lit up goes about the letter for line

parts.note: lit means provided light

explanation.surface: Lighting was set up around a line in a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilt is a light, rhythmic, swinging melody or cadence.

clue.text: Power not seen with second eleven?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for second is not to be seen in the word for power

parts.note: steam is a source of power

explanation.surface: A reserve side of eleven players lacking power.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players.

clue.text: Us importer's 'knitted babywear

indicators.note: knitting works yarn into a new shape, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An American importer's hand-knitted baby clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece garment worn by babies and toddlers for playing in.

clue.text: Confusion over length of time in bulletin

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, over, the second

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Muddle over how long it takes to issue a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts MESS above AGE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official communication or news item.

clue.text: Street in its current form exhibiting inactivity

parts.note: as is means unchanged, in its present state

explanation.surface: A road left unaltered shows that nothing is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium or stagnation, with no movement or change.

clue.text: Assert bridge opponents will get attention

parts.note: in bridge South and West sit as opponents
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Insist that the opposition at the bridge table will be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points: North-South partner against East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear something is to state it firmly and solemnly, to assert it.

clue.text: Wise to include wrecked boat in malicious damage

indicators.note: the word for wise opens to include the rearranged boat

parts.note: sage means wise

indicators.note: a wrecked boat is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clever to involve a wrecked vessel in a criminal act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges the vessel's letters into BOTA; 'to include' means the word for wise holds them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction, done out of malice.

clue.text: Habit one observed in Italian restaurant

indicators.note: the numeral one is seen inside the restaurant word

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A customary practice spotted in a trattoria.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a characteristic or habitual feature of behaviour.

clue.text: Implausible description of peeling plaster?

definitions.meaning: bizarre or unconventional, hard to credit
plaster that has come away from its wall

explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means wildly eccentric; literally it describes plaster detached from brickwork.

clue.text: One affected. following operation

explanation.surface: A patient after surgery is one who has been affected.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a dandy, a man affected in dress and manners.

clue.text: Up and about, shortly wanting wine

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: astir means up and moving about

explanation.surface: Out of bed and soon wanting a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims ASTIR, dropping its R; 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: Hangover cure: 'ere's a priority when drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dropped-aitch form of here's, its letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker insists a remedy for the morning after comes first when sloshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges the whole phrase. The cure is a raw egg with Worcestershire sauce and seasoning, swallowed whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw egg with seasoning, gulped down, is a traditional remedy for a hangover.
